decisions.context: Who: what kind of lender does the underwriter work for, and where? This decides statement formats, regulation and whether "small business" means sole traders or limited companies.
options: UK bank or building society, SME lending desk
UK specialist or alternative lender, or a commercial finance broker
Outside the UK (say where in a note)
decisions.answer: UK specialist or alternative lender, or a commercial finance broker

decisions.context: Who: is this one person's backlog, or a pattern across underwriters? Right now the frame rests on one friend.
options: Just this one underwriter so far
Their whole team has the same problem (they've said so)
I know underwriters at other firms who say the same
decisions.answer: Their whole team has the same problem (they've said so)

decisions.context: Expected outcome needs a baseline: how long does reading statements take on one typical application today?
options: Don't know (I'll ask them to time 3 files)

decisions.context: Volume: how many applications does the underwriter handle per week? This tells us whether the saving is worth the risk to them.
What they do today: what format do the statements arrive in? The agent can only cite transactions it can read reliably.
options: PDF statements downloaded from the bank
An Open Banking feed through a provider
decisions.answer: An Open Banking feed through a provider
decisions.free_text: We can't determine what users will share.

decisions.context: Why now: which purpose-built tools are being phased out or are too expensive, and what does that cost? This claim is our only external trigger.
options: A named product being withdrawn (name it in a note)
Available, but priced above what the firm will pay (give the figure if known)
They've never used one; this is what they've heard
decisions.answer: Available, but priced above what the firm will pay (give the figure if known)

decisions.context: Problem in their words: is "a made-up number lands on whoever signs" the firm's actual reason for banning AI, or our reading of it? And would a version with citations to transactions change the firm's answer?
options: That's the firm's stated reason, and citations would address it
That's the stated reason, but there's also a blanket data/vendor policy citations won't fix
We're inferring the reason; it hasn't been asked
decisions.free_text: It's confidence and price. They want to see a tool working, and they're worried about data being moved out (GDPR risk etc.).

decisions.context: Expected outcome is only readable with real files. Can the underwriter test the agent on real or properly anonymised statements before 2026-11-29?
options: Yes, anonymised real statements, with the firm's OK
Only on their own time with redacted samples, without firm involvement
No; we'd have to use synthetic or our own statements
decisions.free_text: We need to use our own statements and showcase it to get it run with the firm.

decisions.context: Expected outcome: what would the underwriter count as success? Time saved alone, or something about trust as well?
options: At least half the statement-reading time saved, with no wrong figures
They would sign a file using the agent's figures after checking the citations
Their firm would approve it for use on live files
decisions.answer: At least half the statement-reading time saved, with no wrong figures

decisions.context: The real blocker (D7 against the title). The title assumes the firm would hand over statement reading 'if it never invents a number'. D7 says the actual objections are price, wanting to see it working, and applicant data leaving the firm (GDPR). If data leaving the firm is what blocks it, citations don't matter; where the tool runs does. Ask whoever would approve a tool (operations, compliance or head of credit, not the friend) what would block a pilot.
options: Data protection: any outside processing of applicant data needs a DPA and vendor onboarding; a tool that runs inside the firm, with no transaction data leaving, might pass
Price: they have a ceiling per application or per month (record the figure); accuracy comes second
Traceability: figures cited to transactions are what would change their answer, as the title assumes
Nobody beyond the underwriter has been asked yet

decisions.context: Buyer and price (D6, D1). D6 says purpose-built tools exist but cost more than the firm will pay. No product or price is named, and the claim that tools are 'being phased out' has dropped. If the firm won't pay the existing tools' price, who pays for this one, and how much? D1 also merged 'specialist lender' and 'broker'. A broker prepares files for a lender and may not sign the credit decision, which changes who carries the 'my name on the file' risk. Get the product name, the quoted price and who turned it down.
options: Lender; a named product was quoted at a price the firm turned down (record product and price)
Lender; nobody has priced a tool, it's the underwriter's impression
Broker; the lender makes the credit decision, so the underwriter's risk is to reputation, not sign-off

decisions.context: Input format (D5). D5 says statements come as an Open Banking feed through a provider, then adds 'we can't determine what users will share'. The repo reads only CSV and Monzo exports; the README lists Open Banking JSON as 'next' and has no plan for PDFs. An Open Banking feed usually arrives structured and is often already categorised by the provider, which leaves less reading for the agent to take over. PDFs are where extraction errors, the real 'invented numbers', happen. Ask the underwriter to count the formats across their last 15 applications.
options: Mostly Open Banking through a provider (name it, and note whether it already categorises transactions)
Mostly PDF statements uploaded by the applicant
Mixed; at least a third are PDFs or scans

decisions.context: Where the 1-3 hours go (D3, D4). D3 and D4 together imply 15-45 hours a week on statement reading alone, at more than 15 applications a week, which leaves little time for memos and calls; these look like guesses. More importantly, the agent marks anything it can't classify as unclassified and refers it to the underwriter (per the README, card acquirers it doesn't recognise and bank transfers without an invoice reference land in M16). If the time goes on judging unclear lines (related-party transfers, director loans, cash deposits) rather than adding up clear ones, the agent hands the hard part back. Ask the underwriter to time 3 real files and split the time between the two.
options: Mostly adding up figures that are already clear (over half the time)
Mostly investigating unexplained or unclear lines

decisions.context: Can the outcome be read by 2026-11-29 (D8, D9)? The metric is hours per application on comparable real files, but D8 says the test will use our own statements as a demo. Our statements don't look like a small-business applicant's (volume, card settlements, VAT, loans), and the underwriter has no baseline from reading them the usual way. The D9 success bar was also set by the owner, not the underwriter. By 2026-11-29, the honest result is the underwriter's reaction to a demo. Pick the metric you will actually read.
options: The underwriter reads one of our statements by hand, timed, then again with the agent, checking every figure (demo-grade, one file)
The firm agrees in writing to a pilot on anonymised real files by a named date (the outcome moves past 2026-11-29)
Re-scope success to 'the firm's approver asks for a pilot after seeing the demo'
decisions.free_text: Send documents and get demo approval: build a working model to showcase its usability, then get approval to onboard it to the firm. Think of this as a SaaS.

decisions.context: Evidence beyond one source (D2). 'Their whole team has the same problem' is the friend's report, relayed by the owner, so it is still one source. Before building for 'small-business underwriters' in general, talk to at least two underwriters at other UK lenders who aren't friends, and ask what they use today and what it costs.
options: Two or more underwriters outside the friend's firm interviewed and the problem confirmed (attach notes)
They already use a statement-analysis tool and are happy with it
Skip it and treat this as a showcase for one firm, not a market bet
decisions.answer: Skip it and treat this as a showcase for one firm, not a market bet

decisions.context: Why now (D6, volume). With 'being phased out' gone from D6, the only trigger left is rising application volume, and a cancelled weekend in November could be a quarter-end or seasonal peak. Get monthly application counts for the last 12 months from the underwriter's queue.
options: Volume clearly up in the last 6 months, not seasonal (attach the counts)
Steady high volume; the backlog is chronic
A seasonal peak that will ease

decisions.context: Sign "Small-business underwriters lose most of each application to reading bank statements, and would hand that part to an agent if it never invents a number"? lane engineering, risk data, confidence opinion, appetite 2w.

Offline mode and the approver (sharpens D10; raised by offer and moat). Would the firm's approver, not the friend, treat a version that runs on the firm's own machine as outside its ban on generic AI and inside its GDPR bar? Offline mode sends nothing out. With a hosted model, only 'Applicant', the dates and the metrics and policy tables leave (src/cma/graph.py:212-218).
options: Yes: a pilot on real files is possible if it runs inside the firm
Only under the firm's own sign-in and IT approval (name the step)
No: any new tool needs vendor onboarding and a data processing agreement, wherever it runs

decisions.context: The product the firm turned down (sharpens D11; raised by moat and offer). Moat's PASS rests partly on this. If the incumbent already links each figure to its transactions, this tool is a cheaper copy. Name the product, the quote and who turned it down.
options: It already links figures to transactions (record the product and quote)
It gives categorised totals with no drill-down to lines (record the product and quote)
Nobody was quoted; it's the underwriter's impression

decisions.context: The Open Banking provider (sharpens D12; raised by all three lenses). Which provider sends the feed, and what does its output already give the underwriter? Pull one sample. If it already categorises transactions with drill-down to the lines, little reading is left for the agent to take over.
options: Raw transactions only; the underwriter does all the sorting (name the provider)
Categorised transactions, but no totals linked to their lines
Categorised totals the underwriter can drill into; the job is largely done

decisions.context: The memo template (raised by product). Which fields does the friend's memo template ask for, and how many map to M1-M16? Get a redacted blank template. This decides whether the output saves copying or adds to it.
options: Most fields map to M1-M16 (attach the template)
About half; the rest are judgements the tool doesn't make (related parties, director loans, gambling, cash)
The figures are keyed into a loan system, not a memo

decisions.context: The friend's own success bar (extends D13 and D9; raised by offer and product). The owner set D9. After timing 3 real files, what does the friend say would make them use this on a live file? Count checking and copying time, not only reading.
options: At least half the time saved, after checking and copying
Every figure traced so they would sign it, even if little time is saved
A short list of the lines they need to judge, found faster

decisions.context: The demo statement (extends D8 and D14; raised by product and offer). The planned demo uses the owner's own statements. They are personal, the importer reads Monzo Flex as a loan, and the categoriser knows only the synthetic acquirer names, so the demo can't show how much lands in M16. What will the demo run on?
options: A consenting small business's real export, with its written OK
A synthetic trades or e-commerce case from synth.py, labelled as synthetic
The owner's own statements, presented as a demo of the mechanism, not the time saving
decisions.answer: The owner's own statements, presented as a demo of the mechanism, not the time saving

decisions.context: Lenders 2 to 10 (raised by moat). After the friend's firm, how would the next lenders hear of this, and what would one lose by leaving after six months? Moat found nothing that makes leaving costly today.
options: Through the Open Banking provider, as a partner or integration
Through a lender or broker network (name it)
Direct sales, one compliance review at a time
None planned: this is a showcase for one firm
decisions.answer: None planned: this is a showcase for one firm

decisions.context: E1 and E5 ask what the firm's approver thinks. The reply only says 'the IT/compliance team would still need to approve it' and that an on-machine version 'could be attractive'. That is the friend guessing what the approver thinks, not the approver speaking. Nothing changes on E1/E5 until someone who can approve a pilot answers. Who should be asked, and through whom?
options: Ask the friend to pass three written questions to their head of credit or compliance
Ask the friend to introduce the owner to IT/compliance for a 20-minute call
Don't contact the approver before the demo; leave E1/E5 open and present the demo as unapproved
decisions.answer: Ask the friend to pass three written questions to their head of credit or compliance

decisions.context: Several figures in the reply are hedged estimates ('perhaps 9 would…', 'I'd estimate…', 'Assuming we're a direct lender'). Which one should the friend firm up first?
options: E3: the actual formats of their last 15 applications, counted from the queue
E10: time 3 real files with a stopwatch, split into calculating / judging unclear lines / reconciling
E2/E6: the name of the vendor that was evaluated and turned down, and the quote
E4: monthly application counts for the last 12 months
decisions.answer: E4: monthly application counts for the last 12 months

decisions.context: Evidence proposal: confidence opinion → anecdote. anecdote: one source outside the owner (the underwriter friend's written reply of 2026-11-16) describes a 45–60 minute statement review in which 25–45 minutes goes on interpreting unclear transactions. It names data protection and accuracy as the blockers to a pilot and gives a success bar of 60 → 25–30 minutes with every figure clickable to its transactions. All figures are the friend's estimates, not measurements. The owner flags that the reply may be templated (it matches another person's reply section for section, including the same numbers), so even its independence is uncertain. Nobody who can approve a pilot, and no other underwriter, has been heard from. Stay at the bottom of the anecdote tier, and don't move to data until at least E3 or E10 is counted from real files.

Pass/refer/fail in the firm-facing tool (R25). The reply says 'I wouldn't want AI making the final lending decision', the policy thresholds are illustrative (README:127), and the board asked to drop or hide the verdict. The design hides the overall outcome in the workspace and the pack unless the firm turns on its own policy; cma run keeps it. Which do you want for the showcase?
options: Hide it unless the firm loads its own policy (design default)
Show it, labelled as illustrative thresholds, not the firm's policy
Remove the policy step from the review flow entirely
decisions.answer: Show it, labelled as illustrative thresholds, not the firm's policy

decisions.context: Where it runs (Option D, R29). D14 says 'think of this as a SaaS'. The reply says a tool that runs on the firm's own machine without sending customer data out 'could be attractive', and that IT/compliance must approve it. The design is local-first: an installed package, a workspace reachable only from the same machine, and the offline lock on by default. A hosted version later would reuse the same workspace behind sign-in and need a data processing agreement. Is local-first the direction for the showcase?
options: Local-first now; hosted only after the approver asks (design default)
A hosted single-tenant SaaS for the showcase instead
Local for the demo, with a hosted pilot planned in parallel
decisions.answer: Local-first now; hosted only after the approver asks (design default)

decisions.context: First Open Banking importer (R36, R37). E7 is open: nobody knows the firm's provider, and the reply only names TrueLayer, Yapily and Plaid as common. The design builds the UK OBIE v3.1 standard shape and TrueLayer, and waits for a sample before Plaid or Yapily. Which first?
options: None until the firm sends one sample export

decisions.context: Cash deposits (R1, R4, R14). The reply asks to 'highlight ... large cash deposits'. The design keeps every cash deposit out of trading receipts until the underwriter moves it, which understates a cash business such as a café. This is a lending judgement, not an engineering one.
options: Out of trading receipts until the underwriter moves them (design default)
Counted as trading receipts, with deposits above a threshold flagged
Ask the friend during the demo and use their answer as the default
decisions.answer: Counted as trading receipts, with deposits above a threshold flagged

decisions.context: Timing the underwriter (R49, R50). The bet's outcome is minutes per application. The workspace can record locally when a case is opened, worked on and signed off, and report it without applicant data. It measures a person, so it needs their agreement. The design has it off by default.
options: On, once the friend agrees in writing before first use
Off by default; the friend turns it on
Don't build it; time files with a stopwatch
decisions.answer: Don't build it; time files with a stopwatch

options: Tier 1 plus the Open Banking importer
Tier 1 plus the pseudonymiser, so the friend can try a real file
A smaller cut: buckets, click-through and offline lock only

decisions.context: Cash limits (R14, R55, D31). D31 says to flag cash deposits 'above a threshold' but gives no figure. The thresholds file ships illustrative values that the firm can edit, and the workspace and pack call them illustrative. The design default is a single deposit of £1,000 or more, plus any month where cash is more than half of trading receipts. A café banking £1,500 a day would have every deposit flagged at £1,000, which fills the judgement queue. A higher limit such as £2,500 lets a one-off £2,000 injection through unflagged. Which default for the showcase?

£2,500 per deposit and 50% of a month's trading receipts
Unusual for this business: above 3 times the case's median cash deposit, with a £500 floor
Ask the friend at the demo and ship their figures
decisions.answer: £2,500 per deposit and 50% of a month's trading receipts

decisions.context: How to read 'a reader never excuses a torn or tampered log as another writer's append' (D65; R43, P15). A writer adds its entry and then records it as complete. Never: every reader reports an incomplete last entry, so a second window warns of a broken log whenever the first one saves

decisions.answer: Only another writer holding the case excuses, and only after the recorded entries (design default; what T12 builds)

decisions.context: R4: alternatives inside one pattern (verify-53, second major). Since D97 a rule's pattern and its names are scanned separately and the longest match at each start is kept. Keep the first alternative, and say in the design that a longer phrase must be a name or its own rule to count as longer

decisions.context: A repair under lock-file interference (R42 and P15 scope, D99). D99 says that if removing or replacing a lock file still lets two writers append, the log they leave is reported broken, never intact. That holds for appends: two entries claim one position, so the chain or the head record fails there. Dropping a damaged (torn) entry is not an append. It rewrites the log through a temporary file and a rename, so that a crash leaves either the old log or the repaired one. Suppose interference lets a second writer take the case, drop the same torn entry and append, all between the first writer's re-check and its rename. The rename then removes the second writer's entries, the first writer's head record matches what is left, and the log reads intact. The design states this as part of the scope, like a hand edit of the log and its head record together, which only a signed pack's pinned head shows.
options: State it in the design only: under such interference a repair can remove another writer's entries, and a signed pack pins the head it saw (design default)
State it in R42 and P15's scope too, in the next revision
Make a repair an append (the torn bytes stay, closed off and named by a drop entry), so 'broken, never intact' covers repairs too; T12 changes its log format and reader
decisions.answer: State it in the design only: under such interference a repair can remove another writer's entries, and a signed pack pins the head it saw (design default)

decisions.context: R42's 're-check before each write' (verify-54, verify-55; revision 10 scope). An append changes the case's files in up to three steps: the empty head record before the first line, the line, and the rename that publishes the new head record. decisions.context: What a reader reports when one writer waits at the gate while another holds the case (R43, P15; verify-54, verify-55). A check that finds the gate busy tries the case lock directly (D98). If the case is held too, the check does not hold the gate, so it cannot know that one writer held the case through its read. The holder can let go, leaving an incomplete entry, and the writer at the gate can take the case between the check's two looks. This is verify-47's corner, which the gate closes only for checks that hold it. Since D105, T12 names a fault at or before the recorded entries from a steady read, and otherwise claims nothing. verify-55 reads R43 as asking for the recorded entries and the rest as being saved whenever a steady read exists, and failed T12 for claiming nothing. Reporting being saved there would let a check say being saved over an incomplete entry left during a free moment in its read. R43 says a reader of a free case names that entry.
options: Name a fault at or before the recorded entries and otherwise claim nothing. In the next revision, write into R43 and P15 that a steady read gives the recorded entries only when one writer held the case through it (design default; what T12 builds since D105)
Report the recorded entries and the rest as being saved, as verify-55 reads R43; no requirement change, accepting verify-47's corner when a writer waits at the gate
